title: Callum Hudson-Odoi to miss rest of Nottingham Forest’s season through injury
content:
Nottingham Forest winger Callum Hudson-Odoi will miss the rest of the season with an injury.

The 25-year-old suffered a muscle problem after coming off the bench in the 1-0 win over Porto last week.

Scans have subsequently shown that Hudson-Odoi, who was clearly emotional as he limped off the City Ground pitch in the 73rd minute, will miss the remaining five games of the Premier League season, according to sources briefed on the matter.

Hudson-Odoi, who has scored 16 goals in 90 top-flight appearances for Forest since signing from Chelsea in September 2023, will also miss the two-legged Europa League semi-final against Aston Villa.

Forest secured a vital 4-1 win over Burnley in Hudson-Odoi’s absence on Sunday, with Morgan Gibbs-White netting a second-half hat-trick.

In the aftermath, Forest head coach Vitor Pereira confirmed that Hudson-Odoi’s injury was a “serious” one.

Defender Murillo also limped off the pitch in the Porto game and again when named in the starting line-up against Burnley, but Forest hope his issue is minor. Italian defender Nicolo Savona has previously been ruled out for the rest of the season with a knee problem.

Hudson-Odoi has established himself as a key figure with Forest since joining for the cut-price fee of just £3million (now $4.06m).

His value to Forest has been far greater than that, with the former England man having made 43 appearances in all competitions this season, scoring six goals along the way.

Forest spent more than £100m to bolster their attacking options down the flanks last summer, signing Dilane Bakwa (Strasbourg, £30m), Omari Hutchinson (Ipswich Town, £37.5m) and Dan Ndoye (Bologna, £35m), following the £52m sale of Anthony Elanga to Newcastle United.

But, while the trio all have promise, they are yet to consistently make the same impact as Hudson-Odoi and previously Elanga had in the Garibaldi red.

Hudson-Odoi’s experience, as well as his attacking threat, will be missed in the crucial final stages of the campaign.

Gibbs-White’s hat-trick came after he had been shifted into a slightly wider role at half-time on Sunday and that may be a viable option to help Pereira fill the void left by Hudson-Odoi’s absence in the short-term.
